articles.title: Danmark svänger om – förlänger elbilsrabatt
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Danmark svänger om – förlänger elbilsrabatt
articles.body_text: Danmarks klimatminister Samira Nawa. Arkivbild. Danmark svänger om – förlänger elbilsrabatt Danmark gör helt om och förlänger skatterabatten på elbilar med ett år, rapporterar danska medier. Enligt nyhetsbyrån Ritzau gäller det elbilar som kostar över 366 000 danska kronor, vilket motsvarar drygt en halv miljon svenska kronor. Det blir lättare att göra gröna val, och i regeringen har vi tagit hänsyn till att det finns en stor aptit bland danskarna för att köra grönt, säger landets klimatminister Samira Nawa (Radikale Venstre). I regeringens budgetproposition för 2027 föreslogs skatterabatten initialt att upphöra från årsskiftet, vilket skulle tillföra statskassan 800 miljoner danska kronor. Konkret innebar det att man ville sänka gränsen för när elbilsägare fritas från att betala en registreringsavgift. Men efter hårda förhandlingar har man alltså valt en förlängning.

articles.title: Källor: Nvidia överväger att sparka Huang
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Källor: Nvidia överväger att sparka Huang
articles.body_text: Källor: Nvidia överväger att sparka Huang Nvidias styrelse överväger att sparka vd:n Jensen Huang, rapporterar The Wall Street Journal med hänvisning till källor. Uppgifterna kommer till följd av de otrohetsskandaler Nvidia-toppen kopplats till. De senaste veckorna har varit stormiga för chipjättens vd. Efter att det blivit känt att Huang haft en affär med en spionanklagad kvinna har både utredningar och stämningar riktats mot honom. Enligt The Wall Street Journal väntas Nvidias styrelse inom kort hålla ett sammanträde där Huangs framtid som vd ska avgöras. I centrum för krisen står Jensens Huangs relation med Alice Huang, utåt sett grundare av teknikbolaget Megaspeed som varit en av Nvidias största kunder i Asien. Alice Huang pekas dock ut som en kinesisk spion av amerikanska myndigheter, enligt flera medier. Under onsdagen rapporterade The New York Times, med hänvisning till källor, att Jensen Huang anklagas för ännu en affär. I det fallet med en toppchef inom Nvidia. Nvidia har i omgångar varit världens högst värderade börsbolag, men aktiekursen har dalat i samband med kontroverserna. Den senaste månaden är aktien ned med mer än 20 procent. Jensen Huang är en av chipjättens medgrundare och äger drygt 3 procent av aktierna, enligt Bloomberg . Han har varit Nvidias vd sedan starten, år 1993.

articles.title: Pappersproduktion pausas på grund av elpriset
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Pappersproduktion pausas på grund av elpriset
articles.body_text: Lessebo Paper pausar produktionen på grund av elpriserna. Arkivbild. Pappersproduktion pausas på grund av elpriset Lessebo Paper har tvingats pausa sin produktion på grund av de höga elpriserna. I måndags hade vi en elförbrukning på 390 000 kronor på en dag, säger bolagets vd Jens Olson till SVT Nyheter Småland . Jens Olson är kritisk till skillnaderna i elpriset för de norra och södra delarna av landet. Han anser att det skapar orättvisa villkor för industrin. Regeringen och politikerna måste visa handlingskraft nu, säger han. Hur länge produktionen kommer att stå stilla beror på hur elpriserna utvecklas.

articles.title: Anthropic: Svenskar får delta i noteringen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Anthropic: Svenskar får delta i noteringen
articles.body_text: Anthropic ingår ett mångmiljardavtal. Arkivbild. Anthropic: Svenskar får delta i noteringen Svenska småsparare ser ut att kunna teckna aktier vid jättenoteringen av AI-bolaget Anthropic. Nordnet är en av distributörerna, enligt Anthropics egen sajt . Att svenskar får delta i amerikanska börsnoteringar är ytterst sällsynt. Nu tycks det dock vara på väg att ske för andra gången hittills och inom kort tid. När AI-bolaget Anthropic, känt för AI-assistenten Claude, gör börsdebut den 18 november uppges nätmäklaren Nordnet vara en av distributörerna avseende europeiska ekonomiska samarbetsområdet tillsammans med bland annat Revolut. Dessa två var distributörer även vid sommarens börsnotering av Elon Musks bolag Space X, som därmed blev historiskt som den första amerikanska börsnoteringen hittills där svenskar kunde delta. TT har varit i kontakt med Johan Tidestad, kommunikationschef på Nordnet, som inte har några kommentarer i nuläget. Noteringen av AI-jätten är en av de mest spektakulära på senare år där bolaget siktar på ett börsvärde på 1,4 biljoner dollar, inräknat med personaloptioner och specialaktier. Det är något lägre än värderingen av Space X men i samband med de senaste veckornas oro kring AI-sektorn har förväntningarna sänkts. Företaget har inför noteringen i New York angett ett prisintervall på 70–78 dollar per aktie, vilket innebär totalt drygt 800 miljoner aktier i noteringen. Rättad: I en tidigare version uppgavs fel värde på bolagets börsvärde.

articles.title: Munter stämning på Wall Street – AI-aktier stiger
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Munter stämning på Wall Street – AI-aktier stiger
articles.body_text: Munter stämning på Wall Street – AI-aktier stiger Kurserna på New York-börsen stiger. Halvledarbjässen Nvidia vänder sin sura trend när molntjänstleverantören Coreweave drar med sig AI-branschen rejält uppåt. Ungefär två och en halv timme efter öppning har Dow Jones industriindex stigit 0,2 procent, breda S&P 500-index 1,4 och tekniktunga Nasdaqs kompositindex 2,1 procent. Nvidias vänder sin trend efter vd:n Jensen Huangs otrohetsskandal. Aktien, som föll drygt 4 procent i måndags och ytterligare 5,5 procent på tisdagen, är upp 4,3 procent. Coreweave rusar 23,7 procent på sin kvartalsrapport efter börsens stängning på tisdagskvällen. Rapportens resultat drog även upp ett större antal teknikbolag i Asien och Europa. AI-aktierna Sandisk och Micron tar rygg och stiger 15,8 respektive 13,2 procent. Även branschkollegor som AMD, Broadcom och Qualcomm stiger kraftigt i vågen. Terminspriset på Nordsjöolja (Brent) har stigit 2,3 procent till 93,56 dollar per fat under onsdagen. USA-börserna backade i tisdags efter en rapport om oväntat stora prisökningar i USA i oktober. Nu tror fler och fler att centralbanken Federal Reserve höjer sin styrränta vid mötet den 9 december. Marknaden har nu prisat in 86,8 procents sannolikhet för en höjning med 0,25 procentenheter till spannet 4,00–4,25 procent, enligt analysföretaget CME Fedwatch .

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Australian teen missing in bush for six days rescued alive
articles.summary: The 17-year-old's mum has joked that he is "grounded for life" and "never leaving the house again".
articles.body_text: A teenager missing for six days in dense Australian bushland has been found alive. William, whose surname has not been released, disappeared last Friday while on a camping trip with a friend in bushland about 180km (112 miles) east of Melbourne, Victoria. Extremely cold overnight temperatures had left authorities concerned for the 17-year-old's welfare. Police dogs, divers and helicopters had been involved in the search. He was located on Friday morning and reunited with his relieved family, who said he was uninjured but "grounded for life". Rescuers winched William to safety, and fed him a doughnut and a bottle of water, before he was taken to hospital for a check up. The boy's mother, Elizabeth Barkley, told reporters the teenager had "only a few scratches" and seemed fit and healthy. "He's doing fine, everything seems to be fine, he's in perfect health," she added. "He just stayed in one spot and waited to be rescued and I'm just over the moon he's alive." Joking, she added: "He's never leaving the house again." Police have said officers were emotional to have found the teen alive. "It doesn't happen all the time," Victoria Police Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said. "I'm sure he's got a story to tell us soon, which we're very keen to hear," he added.

articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
articles.summary: Colom is the first black person from the southern state elected to the US Senate in over 140 years.
articles.body_text: Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS. Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. articles.title: Famed ship SS United States to be sunk off coast of Florida
articles.summary: Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner to be preserved and turned into a museum, but it will now become the world's largest artificial ocean reef.
articles.body_text: A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic will be sunk off the coast of Florida and turned into the world's largest artificial ocean reef. The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will soon become a home for sealife and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts. Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum. Instead, after being purchased by a Florida county, it will be added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, as a land-based museum detailing the ship's history is also planned. Before its retirement, the SS United States was known for carrying royalty and celebrities from the US the Europe, beginning in 1952 and ending in 1969. A young Bill Clinton, before he was president, used the ship to cross the Atlantic. Former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy also travelled on the vessel. The ship was moved from Philadelphia to Alabama last year for cleaning and remediation work. On Monday, it took its final journey from Alabama to the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will be sunk on Wednesday in a precision operation without explosives. Stars including Marlon Brando, Coco Chanel, Duke Ellington, Salvador Dali, Walt Disney, Judy Garland and Cary Grant also boarded the ship during its sailing lifetime. Before its purchase by the municipal Florida government, a number of proposals that would have seen the ship live a second life as a museum or a floating hotel failed. Instead, the famed ship sat at various docks with various owners as legal battles played out. The SS United States Conservancy group repeatedly attempted to keep the ship above water, but was unsuccessful. Conservancy President Susan Gibbs - whose grandfather helped design the SS United States - said she was glad that the story of the ship would live on.

articles.title: Missing 11-month-old baby rescued after being buried alive in a crate in South Carolina
articles.summary: Officials say the child was found close to his father's home on Tuesday, a day after he was taken, and is being cared for in hospital.
articles.body_text: An 11-month-old baby has been rescued in South Carolina after officials say he was buried alive in a crate by his father. Koah Sharpe had been missing since Monday when he was taken by his father, Michael Comer, 25, according to the Lexington County Sheriff's Department. Comer was arrested on a burglary charge on Monday evening but his son was not with him. The baby was found on Tuesday "buried alive" and "clinging to life" not far from his father's house, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours. The child is now in hospital receiving care, Koon said, adding he was hopeful he would make a full recovery. Police are still deciding what further charges to bring against the father. The search for baby Koah began on Monday after his father took him from his mother's house. Comer's mother was watching the child and had left her son alone with him briefly, Koon said, when he left abruptly with Koah. Comer was seen travelling to multiple locations without the baby and was later arrested in Lexington County without Koah. A search party of 100 police and fire department officials were then sent to search for the child, the sheriff said. He added that when they asked Comer where his son was, he "did not have much to say" about his whereabouts. Koon said that rescuers searched the woods near Comer's house and saw some "freshly disturbed dirt". As they began to dig, they heard a baby crying - something the sheriff described as "the most joyful sound you ever heard". "The race was on. Everybody was getting down there trying to get him out," Koon added. He said the crate was wrapped in a towel that probably provided enough air for Koah to survive for as long as he did, while the cold weather kept him from getting too hot.

articles.body_text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports. CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal. Bessent has been at the forefront of efforts to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a wider economic blockade. While the exact nature of the threats against Bessent remain unclear, US intelligence has warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans, including US officials. "After the Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase," a source told CBS. Georgetown is an affluent part of Washington that is home to a number of government officials and prominent residents. Those security concerns, the source added, prompted authorities to move Bessent to a military base in the area. In a statement, a Treasury Department spokesperson said only that Bessent "will not be deterred" by threats and "remains committed" to the US effort to pressure Iran's economy. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment. In September, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans. The New York Times has reported that the Iranian effort includes the targeting of current and former US officials. One source told the newspaper this has "reached a more advanced stage". Other US officials reportedly on Iran's list of potential targets include former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former National Security Advisor John Bolton and Mark Milley, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

articles.title: Gibran Rakabuming Raka: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.summary: The news comes at a turbulent time for Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
articles.body_text: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power. It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid. The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran. The aide, Budi Arie, said Gibran's resignation letter was submitted directly to Prabowo on Wednesday. It remains unclear if it has been accepted. Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office. Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials. Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated. "No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said. It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion. Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school. On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said. Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
articles.summary: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
articles.body_text: Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day. Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion. However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible. Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said. After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky. The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe. For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member. For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion. Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system. That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence.

articles.body_text: A 74-year-old Italian man who was found guilty of a kidnapping carried out by a far-left militant group in the 1970s has escaped while under house arrest in Argentina and is on the run. Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires. His escape was not immediately registered because he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor so that it continued to transmit body temperature measurements even after he had prised it open and absconded. Bertulazzi already spent decades as a fugitive after he was sentenced in absentia in Italy for the 1977 kidnapping of Italian naval engineer Pietro Costa. He was awaiting extradition to Italy and was being monitored by the Argentine ministry of security through an ankle tag which registers the wearer's body temperature and movements. Officials said that they had become suspicious when they noticed that the tag had remained stationary. When they entered the fifth-floor apartment in the centre of Buenos Aires, Bertulazzi was gone, but the ankle monitor remained. Wary of Bertulazzi's past with the Marxist guerilla group the Red Brigades and his bomb-making skills, police called in explosives experts in case it had been rigged to detonate, according to Argentine newspaper Clarín. However, the experts found that while Bertulazzi had tampered with the device, he had done so to prevent the alarm from sounding once he removed it. Italian media say that his extradition to Italy had been imminent after his last appeal was rejected. Bertulazzi was first arrested after using a false passport to cross into Argentina from neighbouring Chile in 2002. However, he was granted refugee status in 2004 and lived freely in the South American country until his re-arrest in 2024, when the current right-wing president, Javier Milei, took office.

articles.body_text: Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there." She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

articles.title: Schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
articles.summary: More than 6,000 Italian schools received a threat. Authorities in all three countries say there appears to be no risk to the public.
articles.body_text: Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities. In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger". "These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook. Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected. "As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said. Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated. "Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said. Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected. The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools. The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project. Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

articles.summary: León XIV se despide de Argentina y expresa su gratitud por la acogida de los fieles durante su visita apostólica.
articles.body_text: “Gracias por recibirme con tanto cariño, me he sentido como en casa”, así se despidió este miércoles León XIV de Argentina tras celebrar una misa ante dos millones de fieles en el santuario de Nuestra Señora de Luján. “Queridos hermanos y hermanas: doy gracias a Dios por lo vivido en mi visita a este país, cuna de nuestro querido papa Francisco. Exclamó ante la multitud que llegó al santuario de la patrona del país: “¡Gracias Argentina por recibirme con los brazos abiertos!”, después de haber pasado tres días en el país y visitar Córdoba además de la capital. “La imagen de la Virgen de Luján que hoy nos acompaña llegó a estas tierras en una carreta y ya no quiso continuar su camino, se quedó para siempre con ustedes. El Sucesor de Pedro hoy debe seguir su misión en otros lugares, allí donde el Señor lo envía, pero quiere decirles que los lleva a todos en su corazón”, añadió. Y continuó: “Que Dios bendiga esta tierra de María Inmaculada, cuyo manto celeste y blanco se quedó en los colores de su bandera. articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: El dólar cierra en S/3,40 pese a fortaleza de la divisa estadounidense a nivel global
articles.summary: El precio del dólar cerró este miércoles en S/3,409 en el mercado interbancario peruano, por debajo de los S/3,413 de la jornada anterior, con una caída de 0,12%.
articles.body_text: El precio del dólar cerró este miércoles en S/3,409 en el mercado interbancario peruano, por debajo de los S/3,413 de la jornada anterior, con una caída de 0,12%. El sol logró apreciarse pese al fortalecimiento de la moneda estadounidense a nivel internacional, impulsado por las expectativas de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal (Fed) ante la persistencia de las presiones inflacionarias. “El Índice del Dólar Estadounidense (DXY) avanzó 0,66%, hasta los 102.889 puntos, mientras el mercado asigna una probabilidad cercana al 87% a un incremento de 25 puntos básicos en las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal en diciembre. Este escenario fortalece al dólar frente a sus principales pares, aunque el sol peruano logró mantener una ligera apreciación durante la jornada”, explicó Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista. En los mercados internacionales, el oro retrocedió 0,97%, hasta US$3,992.66 por onza, mientras la plata avanzó 0,80% y el cobre subió 0,19%. Por su parte, el petróleo WTI aumentó 1,22%, hasta US$87,09 por barril. Wall Street también registró ganancias, con un avance de 2.87% en el Nasdaq 100, de 1,63% en el S&P 500 y de 0,40% en el Dow Jones. En América Latina, el peso colombiano se apreció 0,72% y el real brasileño ganó 0,39%. En el mercado local, el tipo de cambio fluctuó entre S/3,408 y S/3,413, con un volumen negociado de US$262.7 millones. La cotización mantuvo una tendencia bajista durante la sesión, en contraste con el avance del dólar frente a otras monedas internacionales, como el euro, que retrocedió 0,65%, la libra esterlina (-0,49%) y el yen japonés (-0,70%). De cara a las próximas jornadas, el análisis de Kambista señala que las expectativas sobre las decisiones de la Reserva Federal y la evolución de los precios de los metales seguirán siendo factores relevantes para el comportamiento del dólar frente al sol. En el ámbito local, la atención estará centrada en la decisión de política monetaria del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR), prevista para este jueves 12 de noviembre, que podría ofrecer nuevas señales sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés en el país.

articles.title: ¿El mes de noviembre tiene feriados? Revisa cuáles son los días NO laborables en Perú
articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Ataques de Ucrania reducen 30% el refinado de petróleo ruso: ¿cómo afectan a Putin y su maquinaria de guerra?
articles.summary: Los ataques de Ucrania han reducido en 30% la capacidad de refinación de petróleo de Rusia, abriendo un frente de presión sobre Vladimir Putin que puede afectar la economía, la logística militar y el abastecimiento interno de combustibles. Sin embargo, el impacto dependerá de que Kiev consiga sostener la ofensiva, advierte el analista internacional Francesco Tucci
articles.body_text: La guerra entre Rusia y Ucrania tiene un blanco especialmente sensible para Moscú: su infraestructura petrolera. Los ataques con drones lanzados por Kiev contra las refinerías rusas han reducido en un 30% la capacidad de procesamiento de crudo del país. Esta ofensiva no solo amenaza con complicar el abastecimiento interno de combustibles, generando impacto entre la población, sino que también plantea interrogantes sobre el daño en el frente militar. ¿Hasta qué punto puede esta estrategia elevar el costo de la guerra para Vladimir Putin y generar presiones dentro de Rusia? De acuerdo con un informe de Reuters, desde finales de octubre Ucrania ha intensificado sus ataques contra instalaciones petroleras rusas. Entre las plantas bombardeadas figuran refinerías de Riazán, Yaroslavl y la región del Volga. Nueve de las 35 principales refinerías del país sufrieron interrupciones operativas o situaciones de emergencia durante la última semana, precisa el informe. Además, detalla que las instalaciones afectadas tienen una capacidad nominal conjunta de unas 300.000 toneladas diarias, equivalentes a 2,2 millones de barriles. En este punto, cabe precisar que la capacidad total de refinado primario de Rusia es de unas 930.000 toneladas al día. Reuters sostiene que a finales de octubre, las refinerías rusas ‌procesaban unas 700.000 toneladas, o 5 millones ​de barriles por día. Dos fuentes de la industria petrolera consultadas por la agencia estiman que la reducción efectiva del procesamiento de crudo podría alcanzar las 200.000 toneladas diarias. Reuters destaca que los ataques agravan las dificultades de Moscú para atender la demanda interna de combustibles. La ofensiva ucraniana se intensificó después de que fracasara el alto el fuego sobre instalaciones energéticas que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, había anunciado entre Moscú y Kiev a finales de octubre. El presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, justificó la continuidad de los ataques contra refinerías como respuesta a los bombardeos rusos contra centrales eléctricas, redes energéticas, sistemas de calefacción y suministro de agua de Ucrania. En diálogo con El Comercio, Francesco Tucci, director de la carrera de Comunicación y Periodismo de la Universidad Peruana de Ciencias Aplicadas (UPC), advierte que los ataques pueden convertirse en un problema creciente para Putin si se sostienen en el tiempo, pues sus efectos podrían extenderse desde el funcionamiento de las operaciones militares hasta la vida cotidiana de la población rusa. Sin embargo, pide tomar con cautela la cifra del 30% y recuerda que Rusia ha demostrado una importante capacidad de adaptación durante la guerra. Para Tucci, la reducción de la capacidad de refinación no significa necesariamente que Rusia esté cerca de sufrir una parálisis económica. “El factor tiempo es clave. Si Rusia consigue compensar rápidamente las pérdidas mediante reparaciones o mecanismos alternativos, el impacto será transitorio y no tendrá consecuencias prolongadas sobre su economía”, sostiene el analista. Sin embargo, el escenario cambia si Ucrania logra mantener una ofensiva constante contra las instalaciones energéticas. En ese caso, los daños podrían acumularse y comprometer progresivamente la capacidad rusa para sostener el funcionamiento de su industria petrolera. “Este tipo de interrupción se puede convertir en un problema que se va prolongando en el tiempo, porque puede afectar simultáneamente los ingresos por combustible, la logística de la guerra y, yo diría que lo más importante, la vida cotidiana de la población”, explica. Refiere que una reducción prolongada del suministro puede encarecer el transporte, la distribución de productos y el desplazamiento de las personas. No obstante, Tucci considera que todavía es prematuro anticipar una reacción social contra el Kremlin. Recuerda que, desde el comienzo de la invasión, una parte de la población rusa, especialmente de los sectores medios y altos, ha mostrado resistencia a involucrarse directamente en el conflicto. Como ejemplo, menciona la salida del país de numerosos hombres en edad militar cuando comenzó la guerra. También explica que el Gobierno Ruso ha desarrollado mecanismos para mantener el reclutamiento de soldados, ofreciendo importantes incentivos económicos a quienes se incorporan voluntariamente a las fuerzas armadas. Para el analista, si los ataques ucranianos se prolongan y sus efectos comienzan a sentirse de manera más directa entre los ciudadanos, podría aparecer un mayor malestar social. Pero advierte que el Gobierno de Putin cuenta con herramientas para contener eventuales manifestaciones de descontento. Considera que el Kremlin podría recurrir a la censura, las medidas represivas y el nacionalismo para neutralizar posibles expresiones de descontento contra el Gobierno. Los ataques contra las refinerías también tienen un objetivo militar: dificultar el abastecimiento de combustible y elevar el costo de mantener las operaciones de las fuerzas rusas en el frente de guerra. Tucci explica que el suministro de diésel, combustible de aviación y otros derivados del petróleo es importante para sostener las operaciones militares. A ello se suma que Rusia debe destinar recursos adicionales a proteger instalaciones energéticas situadas lejos de las zonas de combate. Sin embargo, el especialista advierte que una reducción de la capacidad de refinación no implica automáticamente que las fuerzas rusas se queden sin combustible o que sus operaciones militares queden paralizadas. “Este tipo de ataques presiona la logística y la capacidad de llevar adelante operaciones, pero no las paraliza. Menor capacidad de refinación no equivale automáticamente a ataques inmovilizados o aviones sin combustible”, precisa. Según el analista, hasta el momento no hay indicios de una interrupción generalizada del abastecimiento militar ruso. El suministro puede haberse ralentizado, pero no está detenido. Otro de los desafíos para Moscú es impedir que Ucrania siga alcanzando sus instalaciones energéticas. Tucci considera que Rusia ha destinado parte de sus sistemas de defensa antiaérea a proteger las refinerías y otras infraestructuras relacionadas, pero advierte que interceptar los drones representa una tarea particularmente complicada y costosa. El analista explica que los sistemas de defensa rusos, tradicionalmente basados en misiles y otros mecanismos de protección, no siempre resultan eficaces frente a este tipo de ataques. Pese a las dificultades que representan los ataques ucranianos, Tucci pide no subestimar la capacidad rusa para adaptarse a las condiciones cambiantes del conflicto. Recuerda que Moscú ha enfrentado sanciones internacionales, pérdidas de equipamiento militar y dificultades para proteger sus instalaciones estratégicas, pero ha conseguido mantener la presión militar sobre Ucrania. “Estos antecedentes muestran una capacidad rusa de adaptación extremadamente elevada. Sin embargo, también hay límites”, sostiene. Agrega que Rusia inició la invasión con la expectativa de terminar el conflicto en pocas semanas, pero tuvo que modificar sus estrategias ante la prolongación de la guerra. “Ha perdido muchos tanques y otros recursos, pero sigue en el conflicto. Sigue atacando y causando daños y bajas notables a Ucrania. Hay que tener mucho cuidado con esta capacidad de adaptación que estamos viendo desde el comienzo de la guerra”, señala. Finalmente, Tucci advierte que el prolongamiento del conflicto también plantea interrogantes sobre el futuro político de Rusia y el escenario que podría abrirse después de Putin. Indica que no se puede descartar que una eventual sucesión esté protagonizada por dirigentes todavía más nacionalistas y radicales que el actual mandatario.

articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia has no succession plan and a CEO in hot water, so we’ve drafted a shortlist.
articles.body_text: It’s almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO. Yet here we are, on the precipice of this happening. Over at Kalshi, Jensen Huang’s odds of surviving the week are sitting at a lowly 30% . Even though he built one of the world’s most valuable — and, many would argue, dangerously powerful — companies, the tides have completely turned against him. He has confessed to an extramarital affair, but as of Wednesday afternoon it isn’t even clear whom he meant: Alice Huang, the Chinese executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for her country, or Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports to him and who, five sources told The New York Times in an explosive new report, was also a paramour. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next. While Huang’s 60 direct reports undoubtedly get a closer look, consider this our own parlor game, featuring some obvious and less obvious candidates: Lisa Su . The AMD CEO runs Nvidia’s most credible rival, as well as a distant cousin of Huang. The Information floated her name this week, but why would she leave her job for his? Her company stands to benefit from every day that Nvidia spends distracted by an investigation, congressional briefings, and all the mini dramas that are sure to follow. Her best move might be to send a nice note and keep her current corner office. Eric Schmidt. He was the pick of Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management, who we talked with earlier this week. Schmidt could “parachute in tomorrow and do a very good job,” Sonnenfeld said, and perhaps he could. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, chaired the National Security Commission on AI from 2018 to 2021, and now runs the rocket company Relativity Space. Chips, software, government, rockets — it’s an impressive range. Then again, Schmidt would bring a lot of baggage when it comes to his own extramarital dalliances . It’s hard to see him clearing the board for that reason. Lip-Bu Tan . Intel’s CEO knows chips, and right now he might welcome a very soft landing. Last month, Intel reported third-quarter revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion, then warned its fourth-quarter results would fall short of Wall Street’s forecasts. The AI boom has caused a memory-chip shortage, pushing up PC prices and cutting PC sales. That’s hurt Intel (PC chips are a big part of its business), and its stock plunged 20% in after-hours trading on the warning, having already slid more than 30% since September. A move to a company that’s eating everyone’s lunch would be a pretty amazing escape hatch. Bret Taylor. The former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair now runs the AI startup Sierra, and his resume includes a lot of the biggest brands in Silicon Valley. He co-created Google Maps, served as Facebook’s CTO, and chaired Twitter’s board through its sale to Elon Musk. He then took over as OpenAI’s board chair after the “Blip,” Sam Altman’s firing and fast return. When companies need an unflappable, likable adult in the room, they call Taylor. He probably knows nearly every customer Nvidia has, too. Ian Buck. If the board feels strongly about having a “builder” at the helm, they could do worse than the Nvidia VP who helped develop CUDA, the chip software that has become central to Nvidia’s dominance in AI. Analysts and former employees have floated him as a possible successor, and Kalshi traders give him a middling shot . He’s no household name, but the Stanford PhD seems more viable if Huang can can keep that chairman title and push for a successor he can work with. Someone else down the hall. Andrew Bell, Nvidia’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, arrived 25 years ago as a fresh Cornell grad and has been on an upward trajectory at the company ever since. Like Buck and dozens of other executives who are presumably being scrutinized, he reports directly to Huang. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is the insider most often named, but analysts say she isn’t necessarily a natural successor as an innovator and visionary, and Bell has the chip pedigree. The wild card? Lori Huang . Nobody has floated her, but hear us out: Jensen met his wife as lab partners at Oregon State, so she has been working with him since before Nvidia existed. After graduating, she worked at Silicon Graphics as a micro chip engineer (making more money than her husband, he has said), then scaled back to raise the couple’s family, and she now co-leads the family trusts. If the board wants continuity, they could do worse than a humbler Huang who is also a brainiac. There’s a reason they say that behind every great man is a great woman (and vice versa). articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.body_text: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .

articles.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth | TechCrunch
articles.summary: CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even looking to short-term deals that could lead to higher prices, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings.
articles.body_text: CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings , reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue. CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense. “We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call. Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of the infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion. CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware. Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts. Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge. CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices. The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator. “We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four- and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said. CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.

articles.title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sales of $10 billion represents an almost 50% jump from revenue of $6.7 billion the company recorded in the second quarter.
articles.body_text: OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported , citing anonymous sources. If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year. OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said. OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses. Still, the company lagged Anthropic in catering to enterprises, a market where the Claude maker has pulled ahead, at least in terms of revenue growth. OpenAI has recently benefited from a combination of tighter pricing, discounts, improving models, and a greater focus on building more enterprise-focused products and AI agents that can help people complete tasks. OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50 billion, according to Bloomberg. Meanwhile, Anthropic, which is seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO likely to happen soon , said yesterday that its annual revenue run rate had increased by $10 billion within a month to $81 billion as of the end of October. (Note that OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently: Anthropic counts sales made by its cloud partners, while OpenAI only reports its share of some sales through its partners.) None of those figures are small, of course, but the companies are also competing with models from Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, as well as a plethora of cheaper but still highly capable models from open source AI labs, especially those from China. articles.title: Siri co-founder backs Helix for its voice ID tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in.
articles.body_text: For years, websites have relied on technology like CAPTCHA to prove that the user on the other end is human. More recently, social media platforms have turned to photos or videos to verify users’ identities. Now, a startup called Helix is betting that voice technology can do the same job, without requiring users to hand over sensitive personal information. The voice technology, which can run directly on a user’s device, has attracted backing from Siri co-founder Dag Kittlaus, who will also act as an adviser. The company raised $6.2 million in funding in a round led by Chicago Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Aglaé Ventures, Corazon Capital, Press On Ventures, Tusk Ventures, Yonder Ventures, Rule 30, and Brown Angel Group. The startup was founded by Alex Oberg, Anna Dorofiyenko, and Mike Hall in 2025. Oberg previously worked at Ticketmaster, which acquired his startup; Dorofiyenko led data science teams at Live Nation and Zillow; and Hall has worked at Nike and Tinder, where he helped develop the initial matching algorithm. At Ticketmaster, Oberg played a role in creating Verified Fan, which is designed to keep bots out of the platform. As AI advanced, he started thinking along the same lines for a new solution. “As AI started to come up in the last two years, I was realizing that it’s going to make it increasingly difficult to determine who’s human and who’s not on the internet. Identity on the internet’s always been about proxies for identity, right? It’s your email, it’s your phone, it’s your IP address, it’s your device fingerprint, it’s your device ID,” Oberg said. He noted that with the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in. Its core technology can run directly on a device to determine whether someone is human and estimate their age. The company is also running pilots to explore whether voice can be used as a biomarker to detect conditions such as drunkenness or distress. The company can deploy its technology to replace or supplement CAPTCHA and help block bot attacks. Helix said that because its model can run locally even on an iPhone 13, the cost of deploying the technology is minimal. The startup said one of its customers is Zeel, an in-home healthcare provider that uses Helix’s tech to verify the identities of providers visiting customers’ homes. The CEO also emphasized the limitations of Helix’s technology, noting that it cannot reliably detect whether someone is lying. He added that its voice technology doesn’t identify individual speakers — while verifying them being unique humans — and claimed that even if the company stores a voiceprint, it cannot be used to reconstruct a person’s voice. AI-powered fraud is also a growing problem in phone calls. But Helix believes its technology isn’t yet capable of reliably detecting AI agents during live calls. Siri co-founder Kittlaus said that voice-identification technology has finally reached a point where it works reliably, positioning Helix to scale as AI-powered fraud increases. He also said that Helix’s work to compress its models gives the startup a cost advantage.

articles.title: Databricks' new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With Databricks at 12,000 employees, AI Ghodsi is the first to admit that he can't know everyone and that they are unlikely to confess the things that go wrong to him. But he doesn't need them to. He uses Databricks' newly revised Genie agent for that.
articles.body_text: Databricks on Wednesday unveiled an updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multistep jobs that take extended work to finish. It does this through an ontology that Databricks built to give Genie the context it needs from the information that customers store on the Databricks platform. Corporate leaders can now assign the agent a wide range of tasks, and it will complete them unsupervised, the company says. To prove the point, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses it internally. Instead of a product demo, he fired up his actual agent and walked me through his most recent chats and charts. He showed me how it analyzed the parts of an employee satisfaction survey where the company didn’t score well, and how it helped him rate (and discard) fixes for those low scores that some executives suggested. He showed me how it summarized a big sales pitch to a prospect that went poorly — including the features the prospect said it needed before buying. It also prepped him for a podcast interview by reviewing his previous appearances and developing likely questions. While we talked, he even had it tell him what he should say to me. (And its advice on that wasn’t bad.) The fascinating part was that Ghodsi was using Genie to find the stuff that he’s now unlikely to hear as the big boss. It was a source of unvarnished truth about what wasn’t going well that he needed to address. “Have you heard of Dunbar’s number? The magic number is 150,” he said when I pointed this out. Named for British anthropologist Robin Dunbar, it’s theoretically the maximum number of people with whom humans can maintain stable relationships. In a small startup, a CEO knows everyone, has direct relationships with them, and they feel safe to tell him negative info straight up. With 12,000 employees, Ghodsi is the first to admit he can’t know everyone. At that size, a salesperson isn’t likely to confess a disastrous sales call to the CEO. An HR manager isn’t likely to confess that their idea for increasing employee satisfaction will probably fail. “Anyone who has more than 150 employees, which is a lot of companies, a lot of people can get value out of this,” he said of AI agents generally and his product, Genie, specifically. Ghodsi’s own use of Genie (often called dogfooding, from the phrase “eating your own dogfood”) is one reason why Databricks is now pitching it as an always-on agent for business leaders. He says he also uses it in his personal life, rather than a security-questionable alternative like OpenClaw or Instinct or Muse. He believes Genie can do for the business side what AI, agents, and harnesses (the software that wraps around an AI model and lets it use tools) are doing for programmers. As for the risk that agents will ratchet up corporate AI costs, Ghodsi has an answer for that, too. He said costs can be controlled through Databricks’ Unity Gateway product. It allows companies to set usage limits and to swap in less expensive open-weight models. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission .
